Communicate project objectives, progress, needs, concerns, and deliverable expectations to clients, stakeholders, Project Managers, subcontractors, technical teams, and leadership.
Maintain accurate and auditable field documentation, correspondence, notebooks, technical files, and project records.
Mentor junior staff and provide technical guidance to project teams.
Evaluate new technologies, tools, and techniques for potential use in project execution and Weston service offerings.

Lead EHS compliance for complex assignments and ensure work aligns with Weston’s EHS Program, project safety plans, technical procedures, quality requirements, and applicable regulations.
Reinforce Stop Work Authority, personal accountability, and project- and site-specific safety expectations with staff and subcontractors.
Coordinate with EHS personnel when plans do not align with project scope or site conditions.
Work safely at active and potentially hazardous sites using required PPE, including OSHA Levels D through A, as applicable.

Required Qualifications:

10 to 15 years of relevant experience in environmental investigations, remediation, emergency response operations, or a combination of these areas.
This position requires U.S. citizenship.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in environmental science, Geoscience, Engineering, Physical Science, Life Science, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading complex environmental site investigations or remediation projects involving potentially hazardous substances.

Experience managing field operations, subcontractors, multidisciplinary teams, project scope, schedules, budgets, resources, risks, and technical deliverables.
Experience developing and reviewing technical reports, investigation documents, work plans, field sampling plans, health and safety plans, technical procedures, and quality assurance documentation.
Strong ability to analyze, interpret, organize, and communicate analytical data, monitoring results, and field observations.
Strong leadership, mentoring, client-facing, written, and verbal communication skills.
Experience using field sampling equipment, air and water monitoring instruments, PPE, and related field tools.
Valid driver’s license.

Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910, or willingness to obtain it.

Experience with QAPPs or UFP QAPPs.
Membership in a relevant professional organization.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard business communication tools.

Willingness to travel, complete extended field assignments, and mobilize rapidly for project or emergency response needs.
Ability to participate in on-call rotations and support 24/7 responses to environmental incidents, including chemical and oil spills.

Ability to walk long distances over varied terrain, climb ladders, work at elevation, and lift and carry up to 50 pounds, including field equipment and PPE.

Professional development opportunities.

new_jobs.description:
U.S. Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officers diligently work to safeguard our nation’s heroes and their families from health hazards.

As a professional in the environmental science or environmental engineer field, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer might be one for you.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

As an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer for the U.S. Army, you will identify and evaluate potential health risks and develop a course of action to control or prevent disease, illness, and injury. You may supervise the scientific research for environmental health and industrial hygiene, assess weapons, equipment, clothing, and material systems, and develop policies, programs, and operations to ensure the health and safety of Soldiers and staff. You will attend trainings, continued education programs, seminars, and conferences to broaden your knowledge base, collaborate with other top professionals and interact with the newest technologies in the field.

If you choose to join the Army Reserve, you will be able to serve your country as needed while still supporting your community.

Regardless of how you choose to serve, a career as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer allows you to be all you can be.

Outstanding Benefits and Opportunities

When you join the Army Medical Service Corps, you’ll be making a difference in the lives of our Soldiers and the country at large while gaining access to invaluable opportunities, like supporting humanitarian missions, being part of a dedicated healthcare team, and leadership training, all while earning a competitive benefits package.

Benefits may include:
★ Repayment of qualified education loans to lending institution, paid annually over a maximum of 3 years while serving
★ Based on your field of concentration, you may be eligible for an accession bonus
★ Travel opportunities within the United States and abroad
★ Up to 30 days of paid vacation earned annually
★ Enrollment into the Uniformed Services Blended Retirement System
★ No- to low-cost medical and dental care for you and your family
★ Commissary and post exchange shopping privileges
★ Specialized training to become a leader in medicine

Eligibility Requirements

★ Must have a bachelor’s degree from an educational program accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health with a major in a public-health-relevant field or a bachelor’s degree from a program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology with a major in an environmental engineering-relevant field
★ Must be a U.S. citizen to serve Active Duty
★ Must have a permanent U.S. residency for Army Reserve

Have questions or want more information?

To find out more information about becoming an Environmental Science / Engineering Officer in the U.S. Army, visit www.goarmy.com/medicine. You may also contact your local Army Healthcare Recruiter to learn how you can get started on your journey as an Army Environmental Science / Engineering Officer.

This position performs GIS database maintenance, map production, spatial analysis, application support, and field data collection using Trimble GPS equipment. The role includes both office and field work to ensure Town infrastructure assets are accurately mapped and maintained.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

GIS Data Management
• Maintain and update enterprise GIS databases and geodatabases.
• Edit and manage utility, transportation, stormwater, and other municipal GIS layers.
• Perform QA/QC to ensure data accuracy and consistency.
• Integrate data from as-built plans, surveys, engineering drawings, GPS field collection, and departmental records.
• Maintain GIS documentation, metadata, standards, and procedures.
Field Data Collection & GPS Operations

GIS Application Support
• Support ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, and related GIS applications.
• Assist with the development and maintenance of web maps, dashboards, mobile applications, and field data collection tools.
• Support GIS integrations with Cityworks, Survey123, permitting systems, asset management systems, and other enterprise applications.
• Provide GIS support and training to Public Works and Engineering staff.
Project Support
• Participate in GIS implementation projects and special initiatives.
• Support asset inventory, infrastructure mapping, and capital improvement projects.
• Coordinate with consultants, contractors, engineers, and surveyors as needed.

Knowledge of:

• GPS data collection methods and workflows.

Proficiency with:

• Microsoft Office Suite

Company Description

Job Description

We're looking for a Field Technician with hands-on construction materials testing experience who is ready to hit the ground running. This is an active, field-based role where you'll spend your days on construction sites, road projects, and in testing facilities helping ensure the quality and integrity of critical infrastructure projects.

One day you may be testing fresh concrete at a high-rise development. The next, you'll be collecting and transporting samples between an active roadway project, the curing facility, and the laboratory. If you enjoy working outdoors, being on the move, and playing a key role in construction quality and safety, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Perform standardized field testing of concrete, soil, asphalt, and other construction materials using ASTM and other industry-approved testing methods.

Inspect, maintain, and verify testing equipment to ensure reliable and accurate field measurements.

Communicate effectively with project teams, contractors, and internal staff regarding testing schedules and results.
Perform all other duties as assigned by your supervisor or manager.

Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds regularly.
Comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions and on active construction sites.
Ability to travel between multiple job sites throughout the day as project demands require.
Strong mathematical aptitude and attention to detail.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently while maintaining a high level of accuracy and professionalism.

Preferred Qualifications

Additional certifications related to concrete, soil, asphalt, or construction materials testing.
Experience performing ASTM field testing procedures.
Prior experience working on commercial, infrastructure, roadway, or heavy civil construction projects.

Diverse and dynamic work environment with no two days exactly the same.
Exposure to large-scale commercial and infrastructure construction projects.
Opportunity to build specialized technical expertise in construction materials testing.
Combination of fieldwork, laboratory support, and project collaboration.

Additional Information

Your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

SOCOTEC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The Solutions Engineer will serve as the technical lead for Globalgig customers from the first design conversation through renewal. ▪       Own technical discovery, requirements gathering, solution design, and high-level architecture for single-domain opportunities, including the accuracy of the bill of materials (BOM) and statement of work (SOW).
▪       Partner with Field CTOs to close complex, multi-domain deals by delivering demonstrations, proof of value, and proof-of-concept work, then take ownership of the design at signature, validating configuration, licensing, serviceability, and deliverability before the deal closes.

▪       Lead the technical portion of quarterly business reviews, covering performance and SLA adherence, capacity, incidents and risk, adoption, and recommended upgrades or architecture improvements.
▪       Keep customers informed on new features, software releases, security vulnerabilities, and end-of-life and end-of-support timelines, and turn lifecycle events into refresh opportunities.
▪       Drive renewals and expansion with Sales and Channel teams by starting renewal conversations well ahead of contract end, surfacing out-of-scope requests as new opportunities, and building pipeline across the installed base.
▪       Share structured field feedback with Product Operations on platform gaps and customer needs, and contribute to reference architectures, templates, and playbooks.
▪       Support the VP of Solutions Engineering with additional tasks as needed.
Reporting Relationships:

▪       Direct supervision given from VP of Solutions Engineering
▪       Key Working Relationships: Sales and Channel teams, Field CTOs, Delivery, Project Management, NOC, Engineering, Marketing, and Product Operations

▪       Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience
▪       Deep, hands-on knowledge of enterprise networking and security, including SD-WAN, SASE and SSE, Zero Trust, cloud networking, and endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR)

▪       Understanding of service delivery models, provisioning workflows, and operational constraints
▪       Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex technology in business terms to both engineers and CIO/CISO-level audiences
▪       Strong documentation skills, including architecture diagrams, technical write-ups, and business review materials
▪       Ability to manage multiple customer accounts at once and balance presales and post-sale priorities
▪       Self-motivated with the ability to prioritize, execute, and handle escalations while maintaining customer trust
Preferred:

▪       Industry certifications such as PCNSE, CCNP, Fortinet NSE/FCP, or CISSP (Globalgig supports ongoing certification)
▪       Experience in a post-sale role such as customer success engineering, technical account management, or professional services
▪       Experience with managed service providers or indirect channel sales organizations
▪       Ability to work within a cooperative team environment, as well as perform assignments autonomously
Physical Requirements:

▪       Ability to sit or stand at a computer terminal for long periods of time.
▪       Ability to work remotely, with in-person customer meetings and events as needed
▪       Ability to travel approximately 25% of the time

This role involves generating actionable insights, developing statistical models, and supporting various analytical explorations for both internal and external clients. As a Principal Data Analyst, you will be instrumental in compiling data from multiple sources, ensuring data quality, and transforming data to meet specific analytical needs. You will conduct statistical testing, create visualizations, and provide consultative support to clients regarding data availability, key performance indicators, and reporting capabilities. Demonstrated ability to gather requirements and translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical stakeholders is essential. Candidates must hold the appropriate government security clearance and be a U.S. citizen, as this role involves working with sensitive government data. Preferred qualifications include at least three years of consulting experience, proficiency with analytical tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Oracle Analytics, and strong SQL skills. Experience communicating insights to clients and working within regulatory frameworks will be considered advantageous.

Responsibilities

Compile and analyze complex data sets from diverse sources to support exploratory and predefined analyses.
Audit data for completeness, validity, and overall data health, ensuring high-quality inputs for analysis.
Transform raw data into formats suitable for specific analytical functions or processes.
Perform basic statistical testing and exploratory data analysis to uncover insights and trends.
Create and present data visualizations following established design and presentation standards.
Collaborate with internal and external clients to understand data availability, identify key performance indicators, and interpret analytical results.
Advise clients on Oracle Health reporting capabilities and assist end-users in accessing and utilizing reports effectively.

The Role

The Associate Investment Data Analyst role will be responsible for providing scalable, timely, easily consumable and good quality data for consumption by SAI led products and functions. Develop and implement a repeatable process aimed at streamlining the data sourcing, aggregation, quality and distribution.

We are seeking a highly motivated, proactive professional with excellent data and interpersonal skills who are eager to learn about the Managed Accounts solutions.
1-3 years or more in a data intensive, hands on environment, preferably within investment management or technology industries.

Introductory Fidelity experience; experience with system development projects, business analysis, and data analysis.
Basic knowledge of asset allocation investment products, Performance, Attribution, Fixed Income and Risk related experience.

Basic analytical skills and business judgment.
Intellectual curiosity and commitment to continuous improvement.

The
Team

new_jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Company

Shared Services

Argo and Farm Family are specialty property and casualty insurance brands whose underwriting companies are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Clearbrook Holdings Inc. Argo and Farm Family partner with agents and brokers to provide insurance solutions that enable businesses to manage risks with confidence.

Job Description

The Senior Data Analyst plays a critical role in advancing the organization's regulatory reporting, data quality, and analytical capabilities. This position owns the end-to-end transformation of complex policy, claims, underwriting, and financial data into accurate, timely, and compliant regulatory submissions while driving improvements in data processes, governance, and reporting standards.

As a senior analytical professional, this role combines advanced data analysis, data engineering, insurance domain expertise, and business insight to solve complex data challenges, influence decision-making, and identify opportunities that improve operational effectiveness and regulatory compliance. The Senior Data Analyst serves as a trusted partner to business and technical stakeholders and provides mentorship and guidance to analysts across the organization.

Essential Responsibilities

Design and execute advanced analyses to support regulatory reporting, compliance initiatives, and strategic business decisions.
Transform complex business requirements into scalable data solutions, analytical frameworks, and actionable insights.
Analyze policy, claims, underwriting, financial, and operational data to ensure accuracy, completeness, consistency, and regulatory compliance.
Develop, optimize, and maintain complex SQL queries, data models, reconciliations, and datasets to improve performance, scalability, and reusability.
Partner with Data Engineering and Application teams to design and implement data enrichment, transformation, and integration solutions.
Support and enhance data platforms, reporting processes, and analytical assets using modern data technologies and best practices.
Own data preparation, validation, and reconciliation activities supporting statutory reporting, regulatory filings, annual statement reporting, premium tax reporting, market conduct examinations, audits, and ad hoc regulatory requests.
Develop deep expertise in Property & Casualty insurance operations, regulatory reporting requirements, and statutory accounting principles.
Ensure analytical outputs align with regulatory expectations and support sound business decision-making.
Translate regulatory and business requirements into sustainable data processes and controls.
Independently diagnose data quality, integration, and reporting issues across multiple systems and business functions.
Perform root-cause analysis and develop sustainable corrective actions that improve data integrity and reporting accuracy.
Design analytical approaches for complex or ambiguous business problems where requirements may be incomplete or evolving.
Identify opportunities to automate reporting, improve efficiency, and enhance data accessibility for business stakeholders.
Build strong partnerships with Compliance, Finance, Underwriting, Claims, Actuarial, MGA Operations, Applications, and Data Engineering teams.
Effectively communicate complex analytical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Develop clear narratives that connect data insights to regulatory, operational, and business outcomes.
Challenge assumptions, provide data-driven recommendations, and influence prioritization of data and reporting initiatives.
Champion data governance practices and contribute to the development of data standards, controls, documentation, and definitions.
Establish and enhance data quality monitoring processes within assigned domains.
Serve as a subject matter resource for analytical methodologies, reporting practices, and regulatory data requirements.
Mentor and provide guidance to analysts by reviewing analytical approaches, sharing best practices, and supporting professional development.
Promote a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and analytical excellence.

Qualifications & Experience Required

Bachelor's degree in data science, statistics, business analytics, computer science, actuarial science, finance, or a related quantitative field.
5+ years of progressive experience in data analysis, business intelligence, analytics, regulatory reporting, or related functions within the Property & Casualty insurance industry.
Demonstrated experience supporting regulatory reporting, statutory reporting, compliance initiatives, or financial reporting processes.
Strong knowledge of insurance operations and data structures across policy, claims, underwriting, accounting, finance, or actuarial functions.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and experience working with large-scale relational databases, data warehouses, and data transformation methodologies.
Experience performing complex data analysis, reconciliation, root-cause investigation, and data quality assessments.
Ability to independently manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
Proven ability to influence stakeholders and collaborate effectively across technical and business teams.
Strong verbal, written, presentation, and data storytelling skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in quantitative, analytical, or business-related discipline.
Experience with Snowflake, Python, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytical and visualization platforms.
Experience with data governance frameworks, metadata management, data lineage, and data quality programs.
Intermediate or advanced Property & Casualty insurance designations (CPCU, AINS, AU, API, or equivalent).
Experience partnering with Actuarial teams and supporting actuarial, financial, or regulatory reporting processes.
Familiarity with cloud-based data platforms and modern data engineering concepts.

Key Competencies

Technical & Analytical Skills - Designs advanced analyses, metrics, and scalable data solutions while improving performance, quality, and reusability of datasets and reporting assets.
Business Acumen & Domain Knowledge - Applies deep Property & Casualty insurance and regulatory expertise to connect analytical work with broader business objectives and outcomes.
Problem Solving & Critical Thinking - Independently solves complex, ambiguous problems and develops analytical approaches from the ground up.
Communication & Data Storytelling - Translates complex data into clear, compelling narratives that influence business decisions and drive action.
Stakeholder Management & Influence - Builds trusted partnerships across functions, challenges assumptions constructively, and helps guide analytical priorities.
Leadership & Mentorship - Provides informal leadership through mentoring, knowledge sharing, review of analytical work, and coaching of other analysts.
Data Quality & Governance - Improves data quality standards, governance practices, and reporting controls within the domain.
Strategic Thinking & Innovation - Connects analytics to broader organizational goals and identifies high-impact opportunities for process improvement, automation, and operational effectiveness.

The base salary range provided below is for hires in those geographic areas only and will be commensurate with candidate experience. Pay ranges for candidates in other locations may differ based on the cost of labor in that location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for an annual bonus based on company and individual performance as well as a generous benefits package.

Chicago Pay Range: $128010.00 - $152,184.00
Omaha and Richmond Pay Range: $116,382.00 - $138,414.00
Los Angeles and New York City Pay Range: $139,638.00 - $166,260.00

Please Note

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. At this time, we are not able to sponsor or assume sponsorship of employment visas.

If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar state or local law and you wish to discuss potential reasonable accommodations related to applying for employment with us, please contact our Benefits Department at 210-321-8400.

Benefits And Compensation

We offer a competitive compensation package, performance-based incentives, and a comprehensive benefits program—including health, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

Core Values

At Clearbrook our Core Values are Integrity, Collaboration, Pursuit of Excellence and Forward Thinking. These values reflect who we are today and who we aspire to be - guiding how we work, how we lead and how we succeed.

new_jobs.description:
POSITION TITLE (Oracle title)

DATA ANALYST

WORKING TITLE

Data Analyst-OPT (Personnel Data)

SCHOOL/DEPARTMENT

Human Resources-Salary and Information Systems

LOCATION

Crossroads III, Cary, NC

PAY GRADE

Noncertified Grade 26

FLSA STATUS

Nonexempt

ELIGIBILITY FOR EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT

No

WORK WEEK SCHEDULE

Monday-Friday (occasional evenings and weekends) Position is available for a Hybrid Telework workweek

Position Purpose

As a member of the Oracle Processing Team (OPT), this position manages and analyzes data related to any employment status changes in the Wake County Public School System’s (WCPSS) Oracle database and assists in responding to questions received in Human Resources, as needed.

Minimum Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES (KSAs)

Considerable knowledge of Microsoft Office, specifically Microsoft Word, Excel (analyzing data and performing calculations using databases and spreadsheets), Power Point; Google Apps;
Considerable knowledge of interrelated functions between human resources, payroll, and benefit processes;
Excellent customer service and organizational skills;
Ability to communicate clearly and concisely both in oral and written form using a variety of communication techniques and tools to ensure the appropriate flow of information, collaborative efforts, and feedback;
Ability to gather and analyze pertinent facts, arrive at conclusions or recommendations, and present information in an easily understood and reportable format;
Ability to complete complex tasks and minimize errors with attention to detail;
Ability to work in a team environment;
Ability to work independently and complete tasks in the absence of clear direction;
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with school system staff, staff members of external funding agencies, and the community.

Education, Training, And Experience

Associates degree from a regionally accredited college or university;
Two years of experience in Business, Human Resources, or a related field;
Experience in analyzing and researching data based on policies and procedures.

An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job may be considered.

Certification And License Requirements

None

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Oracle (in reference to Human Resource functions);
Experience in a public school setting working in a Human Resources or Payroll department;
Experience using the online state Licensure and Salary System, North Carolina Identity Management (NCID) System, and the NC Retirement System (ORBIT).

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Analyzes and researches Oracle position data and recommendations for employment (e.g., split positions, end dating positions, researching position history to ensure accuracy, etc.) and evaluates results in order to provide solutions and/or recommendations based on research.
Enters personnel information, from multiple sources, into the Oracle database application relating to new hires, rehires, status changes, transfers, resignations, salary, licensure, contract information, longevity, and other relevant employment data.
Prepares appropriate information to be included in Board of Education reports as it relates to the new hire and rehire status.
Collaborates with other Central Services departments (e.g., Budget, Compensation Services, etc.) to ensure employees are set up and compensated accurately.
Maintains workflow records of Oracle data and processing.
Develops a thorough knowledge of salary schedules, pay cycles, and employee calendars to ensure accurate and timely entry of time sensitive personnel data.
Develops a solid understanding of WCPSS employee benefits and eligibility as it pertains to employment contracts.
Maintains effective working relationships with Human Resources Administrators and Specialists to transition applicants to employee status in Oracle.
Communicates employment status and assignment changes with WCPSS’ Compensation Services (Payroll) to facilitate accurate processing.
Processes employment verification, state service years of service, and the transfer of leave balances.
Responsible for ensuring that monthly payroll cycle deadlines are met.
Performs other related duties, as assigned.

Work Environment/Physical Requirements

This job operates in a professional office environment and has a noise level of mostly low to moderate. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, scanners, and copiers. The position, at times, must be able to come into direct contact with school system staff, staff members of external funding agencies, and the community. Work is considered light physical work, requiring the exertion of up to ten pounds of force.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
10/2025

They are not intended to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required by the employees assigned to this position. This description may be revised by HR and approved at any time.

Description Of Work

We’re looking for someone to join our team to support a dynamic student community. The Program Coordinator
advances student belonging and holistic success by coordinating programs, services, and engagement opportunities that support students at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

The Program Coordinator will:

Develop, coordinate, initiate campus partnerships, and implement student programmatic initiatives focused on creating a campus climate of cultural excellence and belonging with a goal of increasing student success, recruitment, and retention.
Monitor and track program expenditures through financial statements, records, and program expenditures.
Hire, train, and lead student support staff.
Collaborate with Student Life Marketing to develop and implement marketing campaigns for Student Culture and Community events.

About Us:

The Office of Student Culture & Community fosters dynamic and supportive environments, provides empowering experiences, and supports all students to strengthen a sense of belonging and holistic success. We cultivate spaces, programs, and partnerships where all Huskers can engage genuinely, meaningfully, and thrive in community.

We advance student success by connecting individuals to resources that address basic needs, support academic and personal development, and build leadership capacity. We empower students not only to navigate campus life but also to shape it.

At the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, we’re proud to be consistently recognized by Forbes as a top employer and recently earned the Lincoln Family Friendly Workplace
certification. We are known for our welcoming, supportive environment, commitment to professional growth, and outstanding benefits. UNL isn’t just a workplace; it’s a place to build your career and make a meaningful impact in Nebraska.

When you join our team as a full-time, regular staff member, you’ll enjoy:

Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick leave, parental leave, and holidays
Comprehensive insurance options, including medical, dental, vision, and life coverage
Employee and dependent scholarship programs to pursue higher education
Retirement plans with university match
A workplace culture that values your time outside of work

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education/experience.

Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Strong organization, time management, and attention to detail.

Ability to build positive and trusting relationships with students, colleagues, campus partners, and student organizations.

Experience generating external funding sources (fundraising, grants, etc.).
Direct experience developing and implementing workshops, programs, and services across a broad range of topics and interests.
Experience supporting programs or services emphasizing belonging, identity development, or student community-building.
Previous experience developing and implementing comprehensive communication and outreach plans.
Experience working collaboratively with varied campus and off-campus entities.
Working knowledge of student development and leadership education theory.

"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

Onsite in Austin, TX. Relocation support included
$150,000 salary, paid weekly
Day-one health, dental, and vision benefits

What if every moment of play could unlock measurable developmental breakthroughs?

At Alpha, education looks nothing like the traditional model. Our PreK program blends play-based curriculum design with real-time developmental data — no rigid lesson scripts, no compliance checklists. You will design adaptive learning themes across every readiness domain, coach a team of Guides to deliver them with precision and joy, and track measurable milestone progress for every child in the cohort.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will spend roughly a third of your time in classrooms — modeling facilitation, observing sessions, and running calibration reviews. The rest is designing curriculum, coaching Guides with specific, measurable goals, and keeping families informed with evidence-based updates. You will see the direct impact of your work: four-year-olds hitting developmental milestones faster, Guides improving their quality scores week over week, and parents becoming advocates.

Coach the Guides. Design the play. Apply now.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead 1:1 and small-group coaching sessions for PreK Guides, modeling techniques, and celebrating measurable wins
Design and facilitate play-based learning blocks that balance SEL, literacy, numeracy, and motor skills, modeling best-in-class practice for the team
Review and calibrate Guide documentation weekly for rubric alignment and actionability, leading calibration sessions to keep milestone progress visible
Prepare family updates and run team huddles that align priorities and reinforce shared expectations toward campus-wide PreK readiness goals

What You Won’t Be Doing

Rigid lesson scripts or compliance-driven routines have no place here — you'll design adaptive, play-based themes that respond to real data
Teaching to a fixed curriculum handed down from above — you own the quarterly and weekly learning design
Working in isolation without feedback loops — coaching conversations and calibration sessions are built into every week
Managing K-12 students on app-based learning — this role is fully dedicated to early childhood, hands-on, in-the-room work

Preschool Program Coordinator Key Responsibilities

Drive campus-wide PreK readiness outcomes through guide coaching, program fidelity, and joyful, data-driven classrooms.

Basic Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Psychology, or related field; Master's or specialized training preferred
At least 5 years of professional experience working directly with children ages 3 to 5, including as a lead or primary teacher in a classroom or structured program
Proven ability to design and implement play-based educational programs or curricula that advance developmental milestones e.g. Montessori
At least 1 year of experience coaching or managing a team of educators with performance accountability
Experience preparing written family progress updates and leading team alignment meetings in an educational setting
Legally authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship
Willingness to work in-person at Alpha Austin campus with relocation support provided if needed

Nice-to-have Requirements

Familiarity with edtech platforms, adaptive dashboards, or digital observation tools used in early childhood settings
Experience with behavior guidance strategies and co-regulation techniques for children ages 3-5

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.
